documents.title: Required Sections: Artificial Intelligence Statements
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Select one of the following three statements that best fits your course', offering permissive, conditional and no-use templates, so the stance is delegates with tiers.
tiers: Broader Use of Generative AI Permitted Within Guidelines
Use of Generative AI Permitted Under Some Circumstances or with Explicit Permission
No Use of Generative AI Permitted
documents.summary: Syllabus-resources page offering faculty three ready-made AI statements, from broad permitted use with citation, to conditional use, to no use. Instructors pick the one that fits their course. The page sets no single university stance.

units.why: The page tells faculty to pick one of three AI statements: 'Select one of the following three statements that best fits your course to include.' It is a syllabus-statement requirement addressed to instructors before the course, so P09; should because the page says statements are 'available' to include.
units.anchor: Select one of the following three statements that best fits your course to include.

units.why: The three statements run from broad permission to a ban, so the university offers named levels of AI use: 'Broader Use of Generative AI Permitted Within Guidelines', 'Permitted Under Some Circumstances or with Explicit Permission' and 'No Use'. This is P05 (named tiers); it describes the menu, so informs.
units.anchor: Select one of the following three statements
units.frag_end: best fits your course to include.
units.policy: The university offers three syllabus statements for AI use: broader use permitted within guidelines, use permitted under some circumstances or with explicit permission, and no use permitted.

units.why: Tier 1 text says 'Use of AI tools is permitted in this course for students who wish to use them', a default permission, so P02, permit, may.
units.anchor: AI tools is permitted in this course for students who wish to use them.

units.why: Tier 1 says 'Students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work', a duty to attribute AI use, so P24 must. It names in-text citations and reference lists but not tool, prompt or date, so P24 not P25.
units.anchor: Students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work

units.why: Tier 1 says 'Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution qualifies as academic dishonesty', making missing attribution itself the violation, so P28 (nondisclosure is the violation) rather than P36, which is about improper use generally.
units.anchor: Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution qualifies as academic dishonesty.
units.fit_note: Also classifies the nondisclosure as academic dishonesty (P36).

units.why: Tier 2 says 'You will be informed as to when, where, and how these tools are permitted to be used', so the instructor decides case by case and announces it. That is P04; informs because it describes the arrangement.
units.anchor: informed as to when, where, and how these tools are permitted to be used
units.frag_start: During this class, we may use
units.policy: Under tier 2, students are informed when, where and how AI writing tools are permitted, along with guidance for attribution.
units.fit_note: Also says guidance on attribution comes with the permission.

units.why: Tier 2 says AI tools 'should be used with caution and proper citation' where permitted. This is a disclosure expectation (P24) in a permitted setting, so should and permit.
units.anchor: they should be used with caution and proper citation
units.frag_start: It is important to note that
units.fit_note: Also asks for caution in use.

units.why: Tier 3 says 'This course assumes that all work submitted by students will be generated by the students themselves', a default ban on AI-produced work, so P01; stated as an assumption, hence modality must.
units.anchor: all work submitted by students will be generated by the students themselves

units.why: Tier 3 says 'Students should not have another person/entity do the writing of any substantive portion of an assignment for them, which includes ... using AI tools', so AI may not produce submitted work: P19. The comparison to hiring a person or company is secondary.
units.anchor: Students should not have another person/entity do the writing of any substantive portion
units.policy: Students should not have another person or entity, including by using AI tools, do the writing of any substantive portion of an assignment for them.
units.fit_note: Frames AI as an outside entity like a hired person or company (P45).

documents.title: Inclusion of Syllabus language clearly stating the level of use of AI permitted in each course at NMSU
documents.stance_why: The memo says 'students must be informed as to the acceptable use, or otherwise, of AI in each course' and gives faculty three options to choose from; it sets no level itself, so delegates with tiers.
tiers: Broader Use of Generative AI Permitted Within Guidelines
Use of Generative AI Permitted Under Some Circumstances or with Explicit Permission
No Use of Generative AI Permitted
documents.summary: January 2024 provost memo requiring each syllabus to state the level of AI use allowed, using one of three options in the syllabus generator. It gives the task-force origin, lists benefits and concerns of AI, and promises faculty training in spring.

units.why: The memo says 'students must be informed as to the acceptable use, or otherwise, of AI in each course', so the syllabus must state the AI level. This is P09; the memo is addressed to faculty, so actor instructor.
units.anchor: students must be informed as to the acceptable use, or otherwise, of AI

units.why: The memo says 'we need to maintain a clarity of expectations for our students', a rationale for the syllabus requirement. P09 fits best (communicating expectations); informs.
units.anchor: we need to maintain a clarity of expectations for our students
units.frag_start: While we figure out this changing
units.fit_note: Gives the reason for the syllabus statement rather than the requirement itself.

units.why: The memo says the syllabus generator and Canvas template 'now contains three options for faculty to choose from'. These are named levels of AI use, so P05, informs.
units.anchor: now contains three options for faculty to choose from
units.frag_start: the syllabus generator and canvas template
units.frag_end: what level of AI use you will accept in your class.
units.policy: The syllabus generator and Canvas template contain three options for faculty to choose from that inform students what level of AI use the instructor will accept.

units.why: The memo says the three choices 'encompass all potential level of possible use', and faculty pick the level for each course, so P04 (the instructor sets the rule).
units.anchor: encompass all potential level of possible use
units.frag_end: No Use of Generative AI Permitted.
units.policy: Faculty choose among three levels of generative AI use for each course: broader use permitted within guidelines, use permitted under some circumstances or with explicit permission, or no use permitted.

units.why: The memo says the language was 'the outcome from a fall 2023 AI task force which incorporated multiple stakeholders'. This describes how the university built its framework, so P56, informs.
units.anchor: the outcome from a fall 2023 AI task force which incorporated multiple stakeholders

units.why: The memo cites benefits of AI, 'enhanced personalization, efficiency and automation, data-driven insights, and increased accessibility and inclusivity'. No type covers general benefits of AI in teaching (P44 is about professional skill), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: enhanced personalization, efficiency and automation, data-driven insights, and increased accessibility and inclusivity
units.frag_start: The use of AI in education offers
units.uncovered_note: The university states general benefits of AI in education such as personalization, efficiency, insights and accessibility.

units.why: The memo names concerns: 'ethical considerations, dependency and over-reliance, equity and access'. It lists several concerns together, so P53 (harms) is the nearest.
units.anchor: ethical considerations, dependency and over-reliance, equity and access
units.fit_note: Also names over-reliance (P43) and equity and access (P51).

units.why: The memo names 'the current lack of effective tools to detect AI content' as a concern. Detection is unreliable, so P39.
units.anchor: the current lack of effective tools to detect AI content
units.frag_start: and the current lack of effective tools

units.why: The memo says 'it's imperative that we approach this innovation with a balanced perspective', a principle for how the university treats AI. P56 (framework principle), should.
units.anchor: it's imperative that we approach this innovation with a balanced perspective
units.frag_start: As we consider how to best explore

units.why: The memo says 'we should seek training and support from each other' and 'Collaboration among faculty can help mitigate concerns'. This supports faculty learning, so P63, should.
units.anchor: we should seek training and support from each other
units.frag_end: from each other, and consider the ethical implications
units.policy: Faculty should seek training and support from each other; collaboration among faculty can help mitigate concerns.

units.why: The memo says 'There will be campus opportunities in the spring for everyone who wishes to participate in this training and support', so the university will offer training. It is tied to faculty support, so P63.
units.anchor: There will be campus opportunities in the spring for everyone who wishes to participate

units.why: The memo asks faculty to 'consider the ethical implications of incorporating AI into teaching methodologies', an ethics expectation for instructors, so P53, should.
units.anchor: consider the ethical implications of incorporating AI into teaching methodologies

notes: No school or computing-unit AI policy found at NMSU main campus (per collect file). Course layer deferred.
